transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
It's my right knee, mainly. It's been aching for a good while but it's got a lot worse lately.
Could you tell me how much the aching in your knee is affecting your daily life, and also whether you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?

It's getting in the way, I'm afraid — I go down the stairs one step at a time holding the rail now, and I've had to give up walking the dog round the park.

As for medicines, there's an antibiotic that brings me out in a rash, though I can't quite recall the name of it.
Could you tell me about any medicines you take — regular ones or ones that have recently changed — and also about any health conditions, operations, or hospital stays you've had in the past?

I take a few tablets — some for my diabetes and my heart, and one for cholesterol at night. I'm not sure of all the names and doses offhand, sorry.

I've had type 2 diabetes for a fair few years, and I had a stent put in a heart artery some time back.
How bad would you say the aching in your right knee is these days: mild, moderate, severe, or are you not sure?
On a bad day it's about a 7 out of 10, so I'd say it's fairly severe. It's stopping me doing the things I used to.
Can you tell me if anything else is going on along with the aching in your knee, and whether you’ve noticed anything that makes it better or worse?

Going down stairs is the worst, and it plays up if I walk any distance. Resting and a paracetamol help settle it.

It does swell up a bit by the evening sometimes, but there's no redness or fever, and it doesn't lock or give way.

How does the aching in your right knee behave over a typical day or week — is it steady or does it come and go, and if it comes and goes, how often and for how long, and is there a time of day it’s usually better or worse?
It tends to come and go — some days are better than others. It's usually stiffer first thing in the morning, and it's often worse by the evening or after I've been on my feet a while.
Could you tell me when you first noticed the aching in your right knee, and what that was like — how it started and whether anything seemed to bring it on?
It's been going on for quite a while now, a good few years I'd say. Nothing in particular brought it on that I can recall — it just started aching on and off.
Is there anything else you’d like to add about your medicines, like anything new or recently changed?
Nothing's changed recently, no. I take metformin twice a day, an aspirin, a ramipril, and atorvastatin at night — those have all been the same for a long while.
What worries you most about your knee, and what are you hoping we can help with at this visit?
Well, the pain's getting me down, and I'd like something stronger for it. And I suppose I'm wondering whether I might end up needing a knee replacement.

Thanks for telling me about the diabetes and the stent — is there anything else from your past health, like other ongoing conditions, past illnesses, operations, or hospital stays, that you think I should know about?
No, that's about the lot as far as I know — just the diabetes and the heart stent. Nothing else springs to mind.
Is there anything else you’ve noticed about your knee that you’d like to add?
No, I don't think so — that's everything I can think of about it.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
